title: ReLoRA restart coordinates and cumulative update rank
hypothesis: Reusing one rank-4 update basis across four restarts keeps cumulative update rank at most four; phase-specific coordinates over one shared overcomplete basis can recover rank growth, but must beat merged ReLoRA and ordinary block-ID controls in actual bytes to establish Mirror-specific value.
physical_object: One shared 32x16 orthogonal update dictionary, or one rank-4 basis in the static-view condition
mirror_coordinate: Restart-specific address selecting a rank-4 column block and phase coefficient matrix
logical_multiplicity: Four low-rank update phases composing a rank-16 final function

task.target: Seeded orthogonal rank-16 matrix; phase p owns columns [4p:4p+4]
task.metric: Final relative Frobenius error, numerical effective rank, actual serialized inference payload bytes and staged restart-state bytes

controls: ReLoRA independent rank-4 factors per phase, merged into final base weights
Static shared rank-4 basis reused with phase-specific coefficients
Mirror shared rank-16 basis dictionary plus phase address and rank-4 coefficients
Native shared dictionary with ordinary phase block IDs and identical decoder

storage.separate_restart_state_metric: serialized unmerged phase factors/coefficients plus basis/address state
paid_objects: ReLoRA merged weights or phase factors

success_gate: Mirror block-address representation reconstructs relative error <=1e-5, numerical rank >=16, actual complete inference bytes <=90% of merged ReLoRA, and strict improvement over native block IDs in bytes, quality or compute. Static basis rank/error is reported as a negative boundary control.
failure_gate: Mirror misses rank/quality or byte gate, or its saved function and coordinate are identical to ordinary dictionary block IDs. Fresh seeds remain sealed.
boundaries: Closed-form synthetic factor-bank screen; no neural network training
No claim about ReLoRA convergence speed
Rank is measured on reconstructed cumulative update, not number of restart phases
Native dictionary/block-ID control receives the same shared basis and metadata budget
